copy.headline: The music in the grocery store is chosen by a psychologist.
You didn't decide to spend 40 minutes in there. The playlist decided for you.
A landmark study found slow-tempo store music increased time in-store by 38%.
items: Shoppers browsed longer and spent 32% more per trip.
copy.citation: Milliman, Journal of Marketing, 1982 - replicated in later studies.

copy.headline: The genre matters too.
items: Classical music in the wine aisle made shoppers pick pricier bottles.
Country in a convenience store lengthened snack-aisle dwell time.
copy.body: The playlist is a targeting tool.
copy.citation: Areni & Kim, Journal of Business Research, 1993.

copy.headline: Scent. Sound. Lighting. Temperature. Cart size.
copy.body: Every sensory input in the store has been tested, measured, and optimized for one variable: basket size.

copy.headline: This isn't a conspiracy. It's a discipline called "retail atmospherics."
items: Taught in business schools, published in journals, practiced by every major chain.

copy.headline: The store doesn't just sell you food. It sells you the mood to buy more of it.
A list is immune to a playlist.
